title: Evaluation of antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) as adjunctive therapy in patients undergoing supportive periodontal therapy
summary: Periodontitis patients require lifelong follow-up care after their active treatment. This usually involves only mechanical measures, such as regular cleaning of the teeth with residual pockets. The additional use of an antibacterial and possibly anti-inflammatory procedure—photodynamic therapy—could have a positive effect on the condition of the teeth (pocket depth, inflammation).

interventions.name:
control group (without aPDT): Follow-up examinations (periodontal status, measurement of aMMP-8) with supra- and subgingival cleaning (mechanical only)
Examinations at baseline, after 3, 6, and 12 months

Intervention with aPDT: Follow-up examinations (periodontal status, measurement of aMMP-8) with supra- and subgingival cleaning, mechanical cleaning, and application of aPDT to pockets >=4 mm
Examinations and cleanings at baseline, after 3, 6, and 12 months

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
at least 6 months in the UPT program
At least one tooth with ST>= 4 mm in each quadrant
No systemic contraindications or serious illnesses
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnant and breastfeeding women
Severe systemic diseases (e.g., uncontrolled diabetes, asthma, endocarditis prophylaxis necessary)
Severe dry mouth or other oral diseases
Previous periodontal surgery or previous use of aPDT
Lack of cooperation
Medications that could interfere with the success of therapy (antibiotics, immunomodulators)
